name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-19S 'Shortstop'
description:
The KP-19S is Kang-Petrov's deep-concealment micro-compact — a KP-19 reduced to its absolute minimum functional dimensions. The barrel is 76mm, the grip is single-stack, and the slide is narrowed to 21mm width, abandoning the double-stack magazine architecture entirely in favor of a flush-fit 8-round single-stack magazine that allows the pistol to disappear into a front pants pocket without significant printing. The trigger is a longer, heavier double-action-only unit rather than the standard striker — 4.2kg pull, longer travel — a deliberate safety trade-off for a pistol designed to live in pockets and bags without a dedicated holster. Total width at the slide is narrower than most wallet cases. Chambered in 9x19mm Standard. The polymer frame uses the same feedstock as the KP-17 but the part is so small that each one feels slightly different in the hand — mold tolerances that are imperceptible in a full-size gun become noticeable in a palm-sized one.

The KP-19S was developed specifically for the GLMZ transit market — a pistol that can be carried on a person moving through ACS scanner checkpoints (which target metal content above a threshold the single-stack 9mm barely clears on a good day) and in environments where drawing from a holster is not a realistic option. The 8-round capacity is acknowledged by everyone as a compromise. Kang-Petrov's marketing calls it 'sufficient for decisive intervention,' which is the most honest thing a firearms advertisement has said in years. At Φ340, it's the cheapest purpose-built concealment pistol in the KP lineup.

The KP-19S has a devoted following among people who would genuinely prefer not to carry a gun at all but have concluded that the alternative is worse. Medical workers who cross contested zones, transit operators, social workers who enter Excluded encampments professionally — people for whom a gun is a last resort rather than a tool of trade. The gun's small size and heavy trigger communicate a certain philosophy: it's not here to start anything. It's here for the moment when everything else has already failed.
specifications: caliber: 9x19mm Standard effective_range: 20m rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic (DAO) magazine_capacity: 8 rounds weight: 0.44 kg
tactical_use: The KP-19S is not a fighting pistol. It is a 'don't die' pistol — a last-resort tool for operators in environments where carrying anything larger is impractical or socially impossible. At 20 meters effective range with an 8-round capacity, the KP-19S demands precise shot placement and an understanding that the engagement will be brief. Experienced users treat it as a contact-range weapon and practice accordingly: two-handed at arm's extension, aimed at center mass, emptying the magazine and creating distance. Nobody wins a gunfight with a KP-19S — they survive one.
cultural_context: The KP-19S's minimal registration requirement — a deliberate Slagworks lobbying victory framed as 'parity for low-income defensive tool access' — makes it the easiest legal gun to own in GLMZ. This has created a specific social layer: the accidental gun owner, the person who bought a KP-19S during a particularly bad month and has carried it every day since without thinking of themselves as 'a gun person.' Transit workers, clinic staff, delivery operators. The gun that hides in pockets and hopes it never has to come out.

story_hooks: A transit operator who has carried a KP-19S for eleven years without ever drawing it finally uses it to stop an attempted abduction in a platform corridor — and the investigation reveals the 'victim' she saved was a courier for a Slagworks black-site operation, and now people who don't want that known are interested in the transit operator.

A KP-19S with a custom grip panel made from what appears to be bone — human, the forensics come back — is recovered from a storm drain in the medical district, loaded, unfired, with no registration trace whatsoever.
